info.name: AI-First SDLC Platform API
info.description:
Full REST surface for the AI-First SDLC Platform backend (Django 5 + DRF).

---

## Base URL
All routes are mounted under `/api/`. Set the `baseUrl` collection variable (default `http://localhost:8000`).

## Authentication — three paths
The platform is multi-tenant. Every tenant-scoped request must carry a tenant context, resolved one of two ways:

1. **Server session (browser path, primary).** `POST /api/auth/login` (or `/signup`, `/accept-invitation`) establishes a Django **session cookie** and stashes `tenant_id` in the session. Postman keeps the cookie automatically. Unsafe methods (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) additionally require an **`X-CSRFToken`** header — the token comes from the `csrftoken` cookie set by `GET /api/auth/me`. **This collection wires both up for you:** a collection-level pre-request script injects `X-CSRFToken` from the cookie jar on every unsafe request, and the login/signup/me requests auto-capture `tenantId`/`userId` into collection variables.
2. **`X-Tenant-ID` header (dev / testing path).** Most read + write endpoints default to `AllowAny` + tenant scoping, so you can hit them without a session by sending `X-Tenant-ID: <tenant uuid>`. The collection pre-request script attaches this header automatically whenever the `tenantId` variable is set. **Admin-only** endpoints (Users, Invitations, Integrations, and the project membership/role actions) and **member-only** endpoints (repositories, onboarding, dashboard, enrollment GET, artifact preview) still require a real **session** — the header alone is not enough for those.
3. **Runner token (companion daemon path).** The `Runner — Companion` folder authenticates with `Authorization: Runner <token>` (set `runnerToken`). The signed GitHub webhook authenticates by HMAC signature instead.

## Recommended first run
1. `Auth → Signup` (creates a tenant + first admin, logs you in). `tenantId`/`userId` are captured automatically.
2. `Auth → Get Current User (me)` — sets the CSRF cookie so subsequent writes succeed.
3. `Projects → Create Project` — captures `projectId`.
4. `Work Items → Create Work Item` — captures `workItemId`.
5. Explore Trigger / Runs / Approvals / Clarifications from there.

## Conventions
- Trailing slashes are **required** (Django `APPEND_SLASH`).
- IDs are UUIDs, carried in collection variables (`projectId`, `workItemId`, ...). Auto-capture scripts fill many of them from create responses.
- Optional query-string filters are included on list endpoints as **disabled** params — enable them in the Params tab as needed.

exec: // Attach the tenant scoping header when a tenantId is set (dev/testing path;
// harmless to send alongside a real session).
// For unsafe methods, mirror Django's csrftoken cookie into X-CSRFToken so
if (!err && value) { pm.request.headers.upsert({ key: 'X-CSRFToken', value: value }); }
} catch (e) { /* cookie jar unavailable — session path not in use */ }

item.name: Health
item.description: Liveness probe. DB-free by design — works before any tenant/RLS context exists.

request.description: `GET /api/health/` → `{"status":"ok","service":"sdlc-platform-backend"}`. No auth, no tenant, no DB.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Server-session auth (DECISION-3). Signup/login/accept-invitation establish a session cookie + stash `tenant_id`. All are CSRF-exempt (no session exists yet). `GET /me` sets the CSRF cookie the SPA (and this collection) uses for later unsafe requests.

request.description:
`POST /api/auth/signup/` — creates a brand-new tenant, its first admin user (`is_tenant_admin=true`), and logs you in. Returns the `/me` payload (`{user, tenant, memberships}`). **409** if the email already exists.

Password must be ≥ 8 chars. On success this request auto-captures `tenantId` and `userId`.
`POST /api/auth/login/` — `{email, password}` → session cookie + the `/me` payload. **401** on bad credentials. Auto-captures `tenantId`/`userId`.

`GET /api/auth/me/` — current user + tenant + per-project memberships. **401** if there's no session. **Sets the `csrftoken` cookie** — call this once after login so subsequent POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE requests pass CSRF.
`POST /api/auth/logout/` — clears the session. **204** No Content. CSRF-exempt.

`POST /api/auth/accept-invitation/` — turns an invitation `token` into a real tenant User + its queued memberships, and logs them in. `name` optional (defaults to the invited name). Public + CSRF-exempt.

Status: **409** already used · **410** expired/revoked/invalid.

The raw token comes from the invitation email (console EmailBackend prints it in dev). Put it in the `invitationToken` variable.
`POST /api/auth/request-reset/` — always returns **200** regardless of whether the email exists (no account enumeration). The reset link/token is emailed (printed to the console in dev).
`POST /api/auth/reset/` — `{token, password}` sets the new password. **200** on success · **410** invalid/expired token. Password ≥ 8 chars.

item.name: Tenants
item.description: Tenant bootstrap — the one un-scoped write. Normally you create a tenant implicitly via Signup; this raw endpoint exists for provisioning/tests.

request.description: `POST /api/tenants/` — create a tenant. No tenant context needed (this is the bootstrap write). Returns `{id, name, config, model_routing, created_at}`. Captures `tenantId`.

item.name: Phases (catalog)
item.description: The phase/agent catalog that drives the trigger picker.

request.description: `GET /api/phases/` — tenant-scoped catalog returned as `{plan, build, remediation}` buckets. Each entry: `{key, label, agent_key, gate_role}`. Send `agent_key` in a Work Item **Trigger** body. Sourced from the tenant's seeded AgentSpecs; falls back to the in-code catalog if none are seeded. Tenant resolved from session or `X-Tenant-ID`.

item.name: Projects
item.description:
Project CRUD (create/list/retrieve) plus a large set of custom actions: memberships & roles, profile, traceability, brownfield onboarding, repositories, API contracts/drift, and the dashboard rollup.

Any authenticated member may create a project (the creator is auto-granted the `admin` project role). Membership/role actions require **tenant admin**; repository/onboarding/contract/dashboard actions require an authenticated **member** (session).

request.description: `GET /api/projects/` — tenant-scoped list, newest first. Fields: `id, name, track, repo_topology, status, created_at`.

`POST /api/projects/` — creates a project scoped to the current tenant. If a session user is present they're auto-granted the `admin` project role (so they can see/select it). Captures `projectId`.

Writable: `name` (required), `track`, `repo_topology`, `status`. `id`/`created_at` are read-only.
`GET /api/projects/{id}/` — a single project.
`GET /api/projects/{id}/memberships/` — the project's role grants (admin only). Each: `{id, user_id, project, role, created_at}`.

`POST /api/projects/{id}/memberships/` — grant a user a project role (admin only). `role` is one of the platform gate roles (e.g. `admin`, `product_owner`, `tech_lead`, `architect`, `qa`, `developer`, `designer`). `role="admin"` grants a project-admin who can approve any gate. Captures `membershipId`.
`DELETE /api/projects/{id}/memberships/{mid}/` — revoke a project-role grant (admin only). **204** on success.
`GET /api/projects/{id}/role-coverage/` — per gate role: holders, whether covered, whether a gate would be blocked (+ note), and whether an admin fallback exists. (admin only)
`GET /api/projects/{id}/profile/` — the project's 1:1 ProjectProfile (the manifest source). **404** if not created yet.

body.raw:
{
  "description": "Rebuild the checkout flow for speed and accessibility.",
  "domain": "e-commerce",
  "tech_stack": ["python", "django", "react"],
  "coding_standards": "PEP8 + ruff; TS strict.",
  "nfrs": ["p95 < 200ms", "WCAG 2.2 AA"],
  "constraints": ["no PII in logs"],
  "glossary": {"SoR": "System of Record"},
  "important_context": "Payment provider migration in flight."
}

request.description: `PUT /api/projects/{id}/profile/` — create (**201**) or update (**200**) the 1:1 profile; each edit bumps `version`. Partial payloads are accepted (only supplied fields change). `project`/`version`/`id` are read-only. A request that sends `description` must send non-blank text: a blank or whitespace-only description is refused with **400** `{"description": ["A description is required — agents rely on it for every phase."]}`. A partial payload that omits `description` is not affected.

`GET /api/projects/{id}/traceability/` — lineage graph: `{nodes, edges}`. Nodes are artifacts (with SoR pointer/url for deep-linking); edges are TraceEdges (`{from, to, rel}`). Each node: `id, kind, phase, type, title, status, sor, external_ref, url, work_item, work_item_key, work_item_title`. The three `work_item*` fields name the work item whose run produced the artifact; they are `null`/`""` for documents adopted during onboarding (no run).
`GET /api/projects/{id}/source-documents/` — brownfield-lite uploads for this project, newest first.

`POST /api/projects/{id}/source-documents/` — **multipart** upload of a static file for brownfield extraction. Form fields: `file` (required — pick a file in the Body tab), `artifact_type` (optional, default `document`). Returns the ingest result. Extraction failures → **400**.
`POST /api/projects/{id}/onboard-atlassian/` — registers existing Confluence/Jira content as SoR rather than recreating it. **400** if the Atlassian capability isn't configured for the tenant.
`GET /api/projects/{id}/onboarding/` — the brownfield onboarding hub state (upload/adopt/register/index/gap in one read). Authenticated member.

`POST /api/projects/{id}/code-intel/` — persist an **already-computed** code-intel result as a `codebase_intelligence` artifact + knowledge chunk. **202** Accepted. Requires repo-manage role (tech_lead/admin) on the project. `repo_id` must be a registered repository. **404** for an unknown repo.
`GET /api/projects/{id}/gap-report/` — the latest gap report (read-through, no recompute). **404** if none built yet.
`POST /api/projects/{id}/gap-report/` — (re)build the gap report from currently registered evidence, then returns it (**200**), same shape as GET.
`GET /api/projects/{id}/api-contracts/` — the project's registered API contract artifact(s).
`GET /api/projects/{id}/api-contracts/{aid}/` — the contract's current rendered body, read-through from S3. **404** if there's no body.
`GET /api/projects/{id}/drift/` — the open drift queue with cross-repo change-impact for this project.

`GET /api/projects/{id}/dashboard/` — `needs_me` (pending gates, clarifications, my runs) + `health` counters + `recent_publishes`, scoped to this project and the current user. **Personalised:** `needs_me.gates` lists only gates the signed-in user may decide (admins see all); `needs_me.clarifications` lists pending questions only if the user is a member of the project; `needs_me.my_runs` are the user's own running / awaiting-gate runs. Lists are trimmed (20 / 20 / 10; gates and questions oldest first), but `needs_me.counts` (`gates, clarifications, my_runs`) are **uncapped** true totals. Gate, question and run rows each carry `work_item, work_item_key, work_item_title`; run rows also carry `started_s` (seconds since the run was created). `health.published_week` and `recent_publishes` go by `published_at` (when it was published), not the draft date. With no signed-in user every `needs_me` list is empty.
`GET /api/projects/{id}/repositories/` — `{repo_topology, repositories}`. Any authenticated member.
`POST /api/projects/{id}/repositories/` — register a repo (tech_lead/admin). `name` required; `role` optional; `base_branch` defaults to `main`. **409** on a duplicate name. Captures `repositoryId`.
`DELETE /api/projects/{id}/repositories/{rid}/` — remove a repo; reconciles topology + default. **204**. (tech_lead/admin)
`POST /api/projects/{id}/repositories/{rid}/set-default/` — make this repo the project's default base. Returns the updated repository list. (tech_lead/admin)

item.name: Work Items
item.description: The unit of work (per-WorkItem DAG). Create/list/retrieve/update, plus phase trigger, human takeover, and the lifecycle rail. List responses are enriched with card fields (`artifact_count`, `owner`, `needs`). (Also `current_phase`, `run_status`; see List Work Items.)

request.description: `GET /api/work-items/` — tenant-scoped list with card fields. Optional filters (Params tab): `project`, `state`, `type` (epic/story/task/defect), `parent`. Card fields on each row: `artifact_count, owner, needs, current_phase, run_status`. `needs` is `null` or `{clarification: true, label, yours}` / `{gate: true, label, yours}` — `yours` is true only when the signed-in user may answer that question (project member) or decide that gate (same rule as the decide endpoint). `current_phase` / `run_status` come from the item's latest run (`""` when nothing has run).

body.raw:
{
  "project": "{{projectId}}",
  "title": "Speed up checkout page load",
  "description": "Reduce p95 to under 200ms.",
  "type": "story",
  "feature_stream": "checkout"
}

request.description: `POST /api/work-items/` — `project` (required, validated against the tenant), `title`, `description`, `type` (epic/story/task/defect), `feature_stream`, `repo`, `parent`, `depends_on`, `assignee`. `state`/`key`/`number`/`external_ref` are read-only. Captures `workItemId`.
`GET /api/work-items/{id}/` — a single work item enriched with `artifact_count`, `owner`, `needs`.

`PATCH /api/work-items/{id}/` — edit **`title`/`description`/`type` only**. `state`, `parent`, `takeover_flag`, and `external_ref` change via their own actions/reconciliation, not here. `PUT` is also accepted.

`POST /api/work-items/{id}/trigger/` — start a phase run (replaces the legacy slash command). Body: `agent_key` (required — from `GET /api/phases/`), `gate_type` (default `phase_gate`), `required_role` (the role that must approve the gate), `user_id` (optional; pre-auth/runner fallback — under a session the actor is the logged-in user and their companion is targeted).

**202** → `{run_id, workflow_id}`. Captures `runId`. Invalid `agent_key` → **400**.

`POST /api/work-items/{id}/take-over/` — human takeover: automation pauses and the developer hand-works the branch (commits reconcile via the GitHub webhook). Body: `actor` (default `developer`), `reason`. Set `"release": true` to hand it back to automation.

`GET /api/work-items/{id}/lifecycle/` — per-phase state derived from runs + pending gates/clarifications: `{tier, nodes, loops, children, parent}`. Each node: `{phase, label, state, run_id, triggerable}`.

item.name: Runs
item.description: Read-only view of phase/build runs, plus the transcript replay and an offline-takeover entry point keyed by run id.

request.description: `GET /api/runs/` — tenant-scoped, newest first. Optional filters: `work_item`, `project`. Each run exposes `agent_key`/`agent_phase` (human-readable) alongside the `agent_spec` UUID — **re-trigger by `agent_key`, never the UUID**.
`GET /api/runs/{id}/` — a single run (status, engine/model, cost, inputs/outputs, timing).
`GET /api/runs/{id}/transcript/` — read-only replay of the agent conversation: `{run_id, phase, engine, cost, turns[]}`. Empty `turns` when nothing recorded yet.
`POST /api/runs/{id}/take-over/` — offline takeover keyed by run id; delegates to the run's work-item takeover. Body same as the work-item variant (`actor`, `reason`, `release`).

item.name: Artifacts
item.description: Read-only registry of artifacts (pointers + provenance, never bodies). Plus a read-through body preview and a gate-respecting manual publish.

request.description: `GET /api/artifacts/` — tenant-scoped. Optional filters: `project`, `phase`, `status`. Fields are pointers/provenance only (`s3_key`, `content_hash`, `version`, `external_ref`, `sor`, ...).
`GET /api/artifacts/{id}/` — a single artifact pointer record.
`GET /api/artifacts/{id}/preview/` — read-through body (S3 draft/snapshot or SoR), never an editor, never copied into the registry. Authenticated member. **404** if there's truly no body.

`POST /api/artifacts/{id}/publish/` — gate-respecting publish to a SoR. **The artifact must be gate-APPROVED first** — otherwise **400**. Body: `target_capability` (maps to a SoR value if known, else unchanged), `destination` (used to build the returned `sor_link`). Returns `{status:"published", sor_link}`.

item.name: Trace Edges
item.description: Read-only lineage edges between artifacts (requirement→PRD→epic→story chains).

request.description: `GET /api/trace-edges/` — tenant-scoped edges `{id, from_artifact, to_artifact, rel, created_at}`. Optional filter: `project`.
`GET /api/trace-edges/{id}/` — a single edge.

item.name: Events
item.description: Read-only, append-only audit ledger. Each row is enriched with a UI `kind` (info/ok/warn/err) and a human `message`.

request.description: `GET /api/events/` — newest first. Optional filters: `actor`, `action`, `target_type`, `target_id`.
`GET /api/events/{id}/` — a single ledger event.

item.name: Approvals (Gates)
item.description: Read-only pending/decided gate approvals, plus the criteria checklist and the decide action that signals the workflow.

request.description: `GET /api/approvals/` — tenant-scoped. Optional filters: `decision` (pending/approved/rejected), `run`, `work_item`.
`GET /api/approvals/{id}/` — a single approval (`gate_type`, `required_role`, `decision`, `approver_name`, ...).
`GET /api/approvals/{id}/criteria/` — the approval's conditions as typed criteria: `{criteria[], met, total, approve_enabled}`. `approve_enabled` is false while a required criterion is unsatisfied.

`POST /api/approvals/{id}/decide/` — decide a pending gate: role check → record → signal the workflow. Body: `decision` (`approved`/`rejected`, required), `comment`, `conditions` (checklist updates; a required-but-unsatisfied condition blocks an APPROVED decision), `user_id` (pre-auth/runner fallback — required only when there's no session).

**403** if the actor lacks the required role · **400** on gate errors.

item.name: Clarifications
item.description: Read-only list of agent-raised clarifications, plus the answer action that unblocks the waiting agent.

request.description: `GET /api/clarifications/` — tenant-scoped. Optional filters: `status`, `run`, `work_item`. A pending clarification blocks the agent on its `ask_human` tool call (no engine cost while idle).
`GET /api/clarifications/{id}/` — a single clarification (`questions`, `answers`, `context`, `status`, ...).

`POST /api/clarifications/{id}/answer/` — project-membership check → required-answer check → record. `answers` maps each question id to the human's answer. `user_id` is the pre-auth/runner fallback (required only without a session). The blocked agent resumes on its next poll. **403** on role error.

item.name: Source Documents
item.description: Read-only brownfield-lite uploads (global list/retrieve), plus the product-owner adopt gate. Uploads are created via `Projects → Upload Source Document`.

request.description: `GET /api/source-documents/` — tenant-scoped, newest first. Fields: `filename, mime, status, extracted_artifact_ids, provenance, ...`.
`GET /api/source-documents/{id}/` — a single source document.

`POST /api/source-documents/{id}/adopt/` — the onboarding review gate: a **product_owner** publishes the extracted draft artifacts. `user_id` required (must hold product_owner). **403** on role error · **400** on onboarding error.

item.name: Invitations (admin)
item.description: Tenant-admin management of invitations. Create emails an accept link; resend rotates the token; revoke disables it. The raw token is never returned. **Requires a tenant-admin session.**

request.description: `GET /api/invitations/` — newest first. Fields: `email, name, status, grants, expires_at, accepted_at, created_at`.

`POST /api/invitations/` — invite a user and queue project-role grants. `email` required; `name` optional; `grants` is a list of `{project_id, role}`. Emails an accept link (console EmailBackend in dev). Captures `invitationId`. **400** if the email is already invited/registered.
`GET /api/invitations/{id}/` — a single invitation (never exposes the token).
`POST /api/invitations/{id}/resend/` — rotate the token and re-email the link. **400** if the invitation can't be resent (already accepted/revoked).
`POST /api/invitations/{id}/revoke/` — disable the invitation's token. **400** if it can't be revoked.

item.name: Users (admin)
item.description: Tenant-admin surface for the tenant's users and the tenant-admin toggle. Project roles are managed under `Projects → Memberships`. **Requires a tenant-admin session.**

request.description: `GET /api/users/` — the tenant's users with their roles/admin flag.
`PATCH /api/users/{id}/` — promote/demote a user's tenant-admin flag. **409** if it would remove the tenant's last admin. Returns `{id, name, email, is_tenant_admin}`.

item.name: Integrations (admin)
item.description: Tenant-admin CRUD over per-capability connections. One connection per (tenant, capability). Secrets are **write-only** — accepted on create/update, never serialized back (responses expose `configured` only). **Requires a tenant-admin session.** Credential-free built-ins (`a11yai`, and `codeintel` since 2026-09-11) are provisioned automatically for every workspace and have no card on the Integrations screen.

request.description: `GET /api/integrations/` — connections ordered by capability. Fields: `capability, connector, vendor, status (connected/not_connected/failed), configured, binding, created_at`.
`GET /api/integrations/catalog/` — the per-capability vendor + field catalog that drives the connect form. Static wiring metadata (no tenant data).

`POST /api/integrations/` — create a connection. `capability` + `vendor` required; `binding` is non-secret config; `secrets` is write-only (never echoed back). Captures `integrationId`. Domain errors return the service's status.
`GET /api/integrations/{id}/` — a single connection (secret never exposed).
`PATCH /api/integrations/{id}/` — partial update. Only supplied keys change; **omitting `secrets` leaves the stored credential untouched**. Fields: `vendor`, `binding`, `secrets`.
`POST /api/integrations/{id}/test-connection/` — validate the vendor is wired + configured (no live network call yet). Returns the check result.
`DELETE /api/integrations/{id}/` — remove the connection. **204**.

item.name: Drift
item.description: Read-only drift records (the Approval-analog for run-less changes) plus the decide action. Role check (architect for contract, tech_lead for pointer/hash) lives in the service.

request.description: `GET /api/drift/` — tenant-scoped, newest first. Fields: `project, artifact, kind, required_role, status, detail, impacted, decided_by, decided_at, comment, created_at`.
`GET /api/drift/{id}/` — a single drift record.

`POST /api/drift/{id}/decide/` — role check → record → reconcile-or-flag. Body: `decision` (`accept`/`reject`, required), `comment`, `user_id` (pre-auth/runner fallback — required without a session). **403** on role error · **400** on drift error.

item.name: Runner — Enrollment
item.description: Local-companion enrollment (tenant-scoped like every other resource). Enrolling returns a **one-time token** shown once — store it as `runnerToken` for the `Runner — Companion` folder. GET requires an authenticated member session.

request.description: `GET /api/runners/` — the calling user's companion enrollments for this tenant. Authenticated member.

`POST /api/runners/` — enroll a local companion for this tenant. `project_id` required (validated in-tenant → **404** if unknown). `label`, `repos` optional. The session user owns the enrollment (`developer_id` body param is a pre-auth fallback).

**201** returns the enrollment **plus a one-time `token`** (only its hash is stored). Captures `runnerId` **and** `runnerToken`.
`POST /api/runners/{id}/revoke/` — stop the companion's token from authenticating. **404** if unknown. Returns `{id, status:"revoked"}`.

item.name: Runner — Companion (token auth)
item.description: The companion daemon on the dev machine calls these with `Authorization: Runner {{runnerToken}}` (+ `X-Tenant-ID` for the state endpoint). **No session/CSRF.** The tenant is bound from the enrollment server-side, never the body. These requests set their own Authorization header explicitly (not the collection cookie/CSRF flow).

request.description: `GET /api/runner/work/` — atomically claim the next dispatched phase/build task for this enrollment (skip-locked). **200** → `{kind, run_id, payload}` (captures `runId`); **204** when idle; **401** on a bad Runner token.

`POST /api/runner/state/{tool}/` — invoke a build-phase platform-state tool over HTTP (no DB on the dev machine). Set `runnerTool` to one of the allowlisted tools: `get_context`, `get_artifact`, `list_artifacts`, `register_artifact`, `update_artifact`, `add_trace_edge`, `log_event`, `list_work_items`, `create_work_item`, `transition_work_item`.

The JSON body is passed as kwargs to the tool (tenant is bound server-side). Returns `{result}`. **401** bad token · **403** tool not in the allowlist · **400** bad arguments.
`GET /api/runner/builds/{run_id}/` — fetch the dispatched BuildTask (manifest + agent body). **401** bad token · **404** run not found · **409** no build task dispatched.
`POST /api/runner/builds/{run_id}/report/` — report the build result; resumes the BuildWorkflow via the build_reported signal. **401** · **404** run not found · **400** on report error.
`GET /api/runner/phases/{run_id}/` — fetch the dispatched phase task (manifest + agent body). **401** · **404** run not found · **409** no phase task dispatched.
`POST /api/runner/phases/{run_id}/report/` — report the phase result; resumes the AgentRunWorkflow via the phase_reported signal. **401** · **404** run not found · **400** on report error.

`POST /api/runner/reviews/{run_id}/report/` — post the phase-08 review verdict; the server-side CompanionReviewProvider's poll parses the findings. Body: `body`, `status`. **401** · **404** run not found.

`POST /api/runner/clarifications/` — an agent opens a clarification for its run (via `ask_human`). `run_id` required. Idempotent by `signature` (a re-ask reuses the same clarification). **201** → captures `clarificationId`. **400** missing run_id · **404** run not found.
`GET /api/runner/clarifications/{id}/` — the companion polls its clarification until the human answers it in the web app. **401** · **404** not found.

item.name: Webhooks
item.description: Signed inbound webhooks. No DRF auth — the HMAC signature is the authentication.

request.description:
`POST /api/webhooks/github/{tenant_id}/` — tenant is in the path; the **raw body** is HMAC-verified against the platform's `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` before anything is trusted.

Headers: `X-Hub-Signature-256` = `sha256=<HMAC-SHA256(secret, raw body)>` (required), `X-GitHub-Event`, `X-GitHub-Delivery`. **401** invalid signature · **400** malformed payload. Set `webhookTenantId` (usually equals `tenantId`).

*Note:* the signature must match the exact bytes Postman sends, so compute it against the final rendered body. Normally GitHub sends this — this request is for manual testing only.
